competitors.details: Fields data loggers, real-time trackers and site monitoring across food and life sciences. Gap: no autonomous recovery; corrective actions remain human workflows.

competitors.title: Controlant - visibility tier
competitors.details: Iceland-based real-time visibility cloud for high-value, high-risk pharma shipments; raised 80 million dollars in November 2023; acquired business-intelligence firm Intenta. Gap: visibility, alerts and data - not simulation, negotiation or auto-execution.

competitors.title: Envirotainer - containers (adjacent ring)
competitors.details: RAP e2 and Releye active containers dominate active air freight and are approved by major airlines; RAP network. Gap: container-level protection only; no lane-level decision autonomy.

competitors.title: PAXAFE - decision-AI tier (closest threat)
competitors.details: Boston-area startup; calls itself a GxP cold chain decision intelligence and quality compliance platform; raised a 9 million dollar Series A in May 2024; argues industry needs 'orchestration, not visibility dashboards'; July 2026 partnership with Peli BioThermal (hardware + AI bundling). Gap: orchestration of human workflows; no SAP-embedded autonomous execution.

competitors.title: Decklar (formerly Roambee) - decision-AI tier (closest threat)
competitors.details: Rebranded on September 10, 2025 as 'the world's only Real-Time Decision AI platform for supply chains' - a direct claim on the same language. Gap: generic supply-chain decisioning; no pharma-GDP-native recovery loop.

competitors.title: TraceLink - network tier
competitors.source_org: Company materials; Supply Chain Management Review interview
competitors.details: Pharma serialization network scaling 'governed AI agents' across multi-enterprise workflows after a transformative 2025; MINT order digitalization. Chief executive told SCM Review in July 2025 that agentic AI, end-to-end digitalization and item-level traceability are transforming pharmaceutical operations together. Gap: multi-enterprise documents and orders; not lane-level excursion recovery.

competitors.title: DHL / 3PLs - execution tier (adjacent ring)
competitors.details: Consolidating pharma specialty logistics through the CryoPDP and SDS Rx acquisitions. Gap: runs recovery with people and playbooks; sells execution, not autonomous software.

competitors.title: Zipline - last-mile (adjacent ring)
competitors.details: Drones deliver roughly 150 essential medicine products across African health systems - cold-chain aware ops; reminder that recovery execution can take physical forms we can simulate. Gap: delivery mechanism, not a monitoring-to-recovery intelligence layer.

solved_vs_open.title: Five claimable gaps (Ch.6.2)
solved_vs_open.details: Gap 1: full recovery pipeline unassembled (no evaluated system connects weak-signal NLP detection, LLM-parameterized scenarios, deterministic simulation, solver re-planning, resilience scoring, HITL governance). Gap 2: no recovery-decision benchmark exists (Jan 2026 dataset monitors only; RecoveryBench-12 would be first). Gap 3: solver-calling agents have no supply-chain guardrails. Gap 4: cascade prediction has never met LLM agents on an enterprise graph. Gap 5: resilience has never been an optimization objective (maximize composite TTR/fill-rate/cost-at-risk subject to cost constraints).

solved_vs_open.title: Net novelty claim
solved_vs_open.details: Every stage of the loop - sense, predict, simulate, act, comply, learn - rests on published, dated, citable work, and no published work demonstrates the whole loop for pharmaceutical cargo. Textbook open research-to-product gap.

Step 3 (12-month window): use the provisional year for pilot evidence and professional prior-art search; convert to full application only if search and business case both hold; abandon gracefully if white space closes. Parallel assets: ledger data, benchmark and calibration methods are trade-secret-able. Disclaimers: not legal advice; nothing asserts patentability.

concept_portfolio.title: C1 SANJEEVANI - Self-Healing Pharma Supply Chain (WINNER)
concept_portfolio.details: Thesis: the closed loop - sense, verify, simulate, optimize, approve, execute, learn - for life-critical pharma flows. Exact problem: alert-to-recovery gap - signals exist days early, yet pharma exporters take weeks to re-plan; excursions, reroutes and tariff shocks compound into stockouts of critical medicines. Agent design: six agents (sensing; verification & scenario; network impact; logistics & inventory; compliance & HITL; audit & learning) on a LangGraph state machine. SAP fit: strongest - IBP scenarios, TM freight re-booking, Ariba supplier risk, HANA GraphRAG; all three theme agent families map natively. Revenue model: SaaS $15k-50k ACV mid-market + success fees on prevented losses; beachhead Indian pharma exporters. Key risk: scope discipline required - the loop must be cut to MVP size. Scores (econ/pain/hack/sap/novel/agentic/res/ip/start/feas): 9/9/10/10/8/10/9/8/9/7 -> 8.62.

concept_portfolio.title: C2 Tariff Sentinel - Tariff-Shock Re-sourcing Agent (designated pivot)
concept_portfolio.details: Thesis: an agent that watches tariff/HS-code changes and re-plans sourcing and routing the day policy moves. Exact problem: tariff changes affect 30% of global supply chain activity; 50% of firms already re-route or re-source; de minimis removal (Aug 2025) reshaped e-commerce customs. Agent design: policy-sensing agent + landed-cost simulator + re-sourcing optimizer + compliance checker. SAP fit: Ariba sourcing shapes + IBP supply planning scenarios; customs-status signals (ICEGATE for India). Revenue model: SaaS per-entity pricing; strong for customs brokers too. Key risk: policy data plumbing is messy across countries; narrower narrative than C1 for pharma judges. Scores: 8/8/9/8/8/8/6/7/9/7 -> 7.90.

concept_portfolio.title: C3 AlertTriage - Disruption Alert Triage Agent
concept_portfolio.details: Thesis: an anti-alert-fatigue layer that deduplicates, contextualizes and scores disruption alerts by decision impact. Exact problem: alert fatigue - overwhelming low-priority alerts (IBM, May 2025); buyers get notified early yet still lose weeks - triage, not sensing, is missing. Agent design: dedup agent + context-enrichment agent + decision-impact scorer + routing agent. SAP fit: feeds IBP alerts / SAP Event Notification shapes; sits above any alert source. Revenue model: per-source pricing; fast to build; weak emotional story for a hackfest final. Key risk: middle-layer product risk - sensing vendors absorb it as a feature. Scores: 7/8/7/8/9/8/8/9/7/9 -> 7.68. Survives inside SANJEEVANI as the verification and prioritization layer of the Sensing agent.

concept_portfolio.title: C4 SupplierGraph AI - Cascade Prediction on the Supplier Graph
concept_portfolio.details: Thesis: GNN + agent what-if on the multi-tier supplier graph - where does this supplier failure propagate? Exact problem: cascade prediction is mature in grids/finance but absent at BOM/supplier-graph level; single-source dependencies (70-90% China API) are structural. Agent design: graph-construction agent + GNN cascade predictor + agent-driven mitigation planner. SAP fit: Ariba supplier risk shapes + HANA knowledge graph. Revenue model: SaaS by graph size; consulting-lite onboarding. Key risk: data collection for real multi-tier graphs is heavy; demo relies on synthetic graphs. Scores: 8/7/8/8/9/8/9/7/7/6 -> 7.55.

concept_portfolio.title: C5 ColdSentry - Excursion-to-Action Cold Chain Agent
concept_portfolio.details: Thesis: from temperature telemetry to GDP-compliant corrective action - quarantine, re-condition, re-book, document. Exact problem: $35bn/yr pharma cold-chain losses; up to 20% of biologics shipments fail on temperature; monitoring exists, action does not. Agent design: telemetry-ingest agent + excursion-classifier + corrective-action planner + GDP documentation agent. SAP fit: TM re-booking shapes; IBP inventory key figures; document trail auditable for GDP. Revenue model: per-shipment pricing; natural expansion of C1 into a vertical wedge. Key risk: requires real IoT telemetry for the strongest demo; simulated sensors acceptable for Round 2. Scores: 8/9/8/8/7/7/6/8/8/6 -> 7.42. Becomes a product module of the startup roadmap.

concept_portfolio.title: C6 PortPulse - Port Disruption Re-booking Agent
concept_portfolio.details: Thesis: sense port congestion/closures early and automatically re-book freight orders to alternative gateways. Exact problem: port strikes and congestion create weeks-long backlogs (Oct 2024 US strike); re-sequencing is manual. Agent design: port-signal agent + congestion forecaster + re-booking optimizer + carrier-comms agent. SAP fit: TM freight order/booking APIs are the native actuation surface. Revenue model: per-lane SaaS; freight forwarder channel. Key risk: narrower than C1; carrier data access friction. Scores: 7/7/8/9/6/7/5/5/7/9 -> 7.18.

concept_portfolio.title: C7 InventoryBalance - Network Re-Balancing Agent
concept_portfolio.details: Thesis: continuously rebalance safety stock and allocations across the network as risk shifts. Exact problem: static safety stocks ossify; lead-time uncertainty breaks them during disruptions. Agent design: demand-signal agent (Chronos/TimesFM) + optimizer (Pyomo MILP) + allocation agent. SAP fit: IBP inventory optimization shapes natively. Revenue model: SaaS by node count; clear ROI math (inventory carrying cost). Key risk: feels like a feature of IBP itself; weaker hackfest drama. Scores: 8/6/6/10/5/7/5/5/7/8 -> 6.95.

concept_portfolio.title: C8 FreightSwap - Autonomous Re-booking Exchange
concept_portfolio.details: Thesis: when disruption hits, agents negotiate and swap freight capacity across shippers. Exact problem: during disruption, capacity is scarce and bilateral negotiation is slow. Agent design: capacity-listing agent + negotiation agent (LLM bargaining) + settlement agent. SAP fit: TM booking shapes; marketplace tie-ins. Revenue model: take-rate marketplace; high GMV upside. Key risk: marketplace cold-start; antitrust/compliance complexity; too ambitious for 1 week. Scores: 8/6/7/6/7/8/4/6/8/4 -> 6.20.

concept_portfolio.title: C9 DemandShield - Demand-Shock Scenario Planner
concept_portfolio.details: Thesis: convert demand shocks (spikes, cancellations) into pre-computed supply scenarios within minutes. Exact problem: IBP what-if exists but is planner-driven and slow; shocks arrive faster than scenario cycles. Agent design: demand-sensing agent + scenario generator + optimizer + explainer. SAP fit: IBP scenario API is the native home. Revenue model: SaaS; strong upsell into IBP shops. Key risk: closest to 'feature of IBP'; differentiation must come from automation speed. Scores: 7/6/6/10/5/7/5/4/6/8 -> 6.58. Q&A: 'DemandShield is essentially IBP scenarios, automated.'

concept_portfolio.title: C10 CompliancePilot - Customs & Trade Compliance Copilot
concept_portfolio.details: Thesis: an agent that prepares, checks and tracks customs documentation under tariff volatility. Exact problem: de minimis end (Aug 2025) forced every parcel through formal customs; ICEGATE outages snarl clearance. Agent design: doc-prep agent + rule-check agent + status-sensing agent. SAP fit: Ariba/trade compliance shapes; ICEGATE signals (India). Revenue model: per-declaration pricing; broker channel. Key risk: documentation-first feel; less agentic-network drama. Scores: 7/7/6/8/6/6/4/6/7/7 -> 6.72.

concept_portfolio.title: C11 DigitalTwin Arena - What-If Disruption Simulation Platform
concept_portfolio.details: Thesis: self-service disruption simulation for planners - run any shock against your network, compare recoveries. Exact problem: digital twins exist in consulting engagements; no self-serve, agent-operated arena. Agent design: twin-builder agent + scenario library + simulation runner + insight narrator. SAP fit: HANA graph + IBP master-data shapes. Revenue model: SaaS by simulation volume; services for onboarding. Key risk: demo-rich but product-light; monetization needs the execution loop to matter. Scores: 7/6/9/8/8/8/9/6/6/7 -> 7.31.

concept_portfolio.title: C12 ResilienceScore - Network Resilience Benchmarking
concept_portfolio.details: Thesis: a Moody's-style resilience rating for supply networks, computed by simulation. Exact problem: resilience metrics are rich in literature but not operationalized into a comparable rating. Agent design: data-collection agent + simulation agent + rating explainer. SAP fit: reads SAP master data; outputs to SAC dashboards. Revenue model: rating subscriptions; certification revenue later. Key risk: chicken-and-egg - value needs network adoption; slow hackfest narrative. Scores: 6/5/7/7/8/7/9/8/6/6 -> 6.44.

concept_portfolio.title: C13 GreenRoute - Carbon-Aware Re-Routing Agent
concept_portfolio.details: Thesis: re-routing that jointly optimizes cost, service and carbon during disruption. Exact problem: re-routes (Cape +10-14 days) spike emissions; ESG reporting pressure grows. Agent design: emissions-estimation agent + multi-objective optimizer + reporter. SAP fit: TM routing + SAC sustainability reporting. Revenue model: SaaS; ESG-reporting attach. Key risk: carbon is a tiebreaker, not a burning platform; weaker pain. Scores: 5/5/6/7/6/6/6/5/5/7 -> 5.71.

concept_portfolio.title: C14 Negotia - Emergency Procurement Negotiation Agent
concept_portfolio.details: Thesis: LLM agent that runs emergency supplier negotiations (price, capacity, lead time) during shortages. Exact problem: emergency buys are ad-hoc, slow and price-gouged during disruptions. Agent design: supplier-discovery agent + negotiation agent + approval-gated deal closer. SAP fit: Ariba sourcing/contract shapes. Revenue model: savings-share pricing (aligns with Verusen-style $34m claims). Key risk: high-risk autonomy story for judges; negotiation liability concerns. Scores: 7/6/6/7/7/8/4/5/6/5 -> 5.95.

concept_portfolio.title: C15 DisasterMesh - Last-Mile Relief Logistics Orchestrator
concept_portfolio.details: Thesis: multi-agent coordination of relief supplies to disaster-hit regions with NGO/government actors. Exact problem: climate shocks (floods, cyclones) overwhelm last-mile relief distribution; theme text names the human cost. Agent design: needs-assessment agent + resource-matching agent + route agent + coordinator. SAP fit: weak enterprise SAP fit (NGO systems are heterogeneous); TM where present. Revenue model: grant/donor-funded; unclear commercial engine. Key risk: emotionally powerful but commercially weakest; hardware-adjacent dependencies in floods. Scores: 5/9/8/4/5/7/6/3/4/5 -> 5.48.

concept_portfolio.title: Scoring criteria and weights
concept_portfolio.details: Criteria and weights: economic value 15%, customer pain 15%, hackfest relevance 15%, SAP strategic alignment 10%, technical novelty 10%, agentic-AI suitability 10%, research potential 5%, patent/IP potential 5%, startup potential 10%, prototype feasibility 5%. Each criterion scored 0-10 from the evidence in Chapters 2-8; weighted total out of 10. Scores are anchored judgments: every 8+ score cites a documented fact; team-capability assumptions flagged. Totals recorded as printed in Tables 11/12.

concept_portfolio.title: Selection verdict and sensitivity check
concept_portfolio.details: SANJEEVANI (8.62) beats Tariff Sentinel (7.90) on the three 15% criteria combined; AlertTriage (7.68) is the most honest strategic insight but middleware with no visible loop. Sensitivity check: if startup potential and IP weights are doubled (venture-first reading), C1 still leads (9.0 normalized), with C4 narrowing the gap on research/IP but losing on feasibility - selection robust to reasonable weight changes. Selection locked: Primary C1 SANJEEVANI; backup/pivot C2 Tariff Sentinel (same architecture, trade-policy anchor); strategic harvest: C3 AlertTriage and C5 ColdSentry become product modules of the startup roadmap.

personas.title: Primary persona: Meera Iyer

architecture.title: Resilience Autonomy Loop - 10 stages with human gate at step 7
architecture.details: The Resilience Autonomy Loop (10 stages, human gate at step 7): the project's visual signature - put it on the title slide, the architecture slide, and the demo HUD. Full chain (workflow PDF p.1): Sense - Verify - Understand - Scenario - Simulate - Optimize - Approve - Execute - Audit - Learn.

architecture.title: Current workflow vs SANJEEVANI workflow (Table 15)
architecture.details: Sense: forwarder emails/news apps/4 dashboards hours-to-days reactive VS continuous NLP + weather + port + tariff + IoT screening, minutes proactive. Verify: planner phone calls VS cross-source verification agent with confidence scores, dedup built in. Assess impact: Excel what-if rebuilt per event 1-3 days VS supply-graph propagation + stockout/cost estimate, minutes. Decide: war-room call VS digital twin replays 3 recovery strategies; optimizer picks best trade-off. Approve: COO sign-off by email/WhatsApp VS risk-tiered gate - low-risk auto-executes; high-impact one-click approval with full context. Execute: planner updates SAP manually item by item VS execution agent posts approved actions to IBP/TM/Ariba-shaped APIs atomically. Comply+audit: investigation report retroactive VS compliance validated pre-execution; audit ledger writes itself. Learn: nothing systematic VS prediction-vs-outcome recalibration after every event.

architecture.title: Seven-band system architecture
architecture.details: The architecture has seven bands. (1) Signal layer, always-on: news and geopolitical screening, weather and climate alerts, port and logistics status, tariff and trade-policy notices, cold-chain IoT telemetry - all free or free-tier sources standing in for the Everstream/Prewave partner pattern. (2) Data layer: SAP HANA Cloud free tier - events embedded in the vector engine, supplier-plant-lane-customer network in the knowledge graph engine, provenance-tagged store. (3) Agent layer: LangGraph state machine running six specialized agents. (4) Simulation band (SimPy digital twin) and (5) optimization band (Pyomo+HiGHS MILP, OR-Tools routing) - deterministic engines the agents orchestrate: the LLM reasons, the math decides. (6) Governance gate: validates every plan against policy, escalates by risk tier to a human. (7) SAP execution band posts approved actions through API-faithful surfaces, and the audit ledger records event, reasoning, scenario, recommendation, approval, action and outcome - the full decision trail the Learning agent replays to recalibrate thresholds.

architecture.title: Approval tiers (cost-banded)
architecture.details: Approval tiers: cost-banded actions - under $5k impact: auto-execute; $5k-50k: planner approval; over $50k or compliance-sensitive: COO approval. Thresholds live in the policy engine, editable per customer.

architecture.title: Policy engine - guardrailed solver-calling pattern
architecture.details: Every tool-call an agent makes toward a solver or an API is validated against parameter bounds, budget caps, sanctions and trade-policy constraints before execution. This is the guardrailed solver-calling pattern (patent hypothesis H4).

architecture.title: Prompt-injection and data hygiene defenses
architecture.details: External text (news) is treated as untrusted: summarization happens in a sandboxed pass; no external text reaches tool-parameters; every parameter is schema-validated before a solver call.

architecture.title: Failure containment and advisory degradation
architecture.details: Agents are stateless between runs (state in checkpoints); any agent failure degrades the loop to advisory mode - the system recommends, humans execute; the SAP systems of record are never blocked.

architecture.title: Rollback design
architecture.details: Execution posts are transactional with compensating actions defined up-front (e.g., a re-booking can be re-booked back); the audit ledger supports replay of any decision for post-mortem. Answer to 'what happens when the AI is wrong': the same thing that happens when a planner is wrong - a documented decision, reviewed by a human, bounded by policy, reversible by design. The difference is speed and memory.

architecture.title: Escalation matrix L1-L4 (Table 18)
architecture.details: L1 - Log: single-point telemetry glitch, dwell inside tolerance -> auto-log to audit trail, no alerts; human role none (visibility only). L2 - Auto-act + notify: projected drift with low-cost in-lane fix (reefer setpoint, pre-cool) -> execute playbook automatically, push notification with rationale; post-hoc review. L3 - Human approval: carrier swap, warehouse diversion, cost above threshold -> console approval card with options, cost, risk, GDP impact; e-signature required; approve or reject with one tap. L4 - Quarantine + CAPA: confirmed stability breach -> cargo quarantine flag, excursion dossier assembled, quality and CAPA workflow opened; QA investigation. The severity ladder keeps autonomy auditable.

architecture.title: All IoT signals software-simulated (policy + rationale)
architecture.details: All IoT signals are software-simulated. The hackfest handbook disqualifies hardware entries outright, and simulation is also better theater - the telemetry stream is deterministic and repeatable, the dwell event can be injected live from the presenter console, and no battery or connectivity failure can derail a six-minute demo. The simulation layer emits the same JSON event shapes a production Tive- or Sensitech-class device would emit - the architecture is honest about being integration-ready rather than integration-dependent.

architecture.title: Component-to-SAP mapping and demo feasibility (Table 17)
architecture.details: Signal ingestion + NLP screening (Python, news/weather feeds, embeddings; stands in for Everstream/Prewave IBP feed pattern) GREEN. Event store + GraphRAG (HANA Cloud free tier vector + KG; native HANA, published SAP RAG pattern) GREEN. Agent orchestration (LangGraph state machine, HITL interrupts; A2A/MCP aligned, Joule-Studio-compatible) GREEN. Digital twin replay (SimPy DES on 12-node network; models IBP planning-area semantics) GREEN. Recovery optimization (Pyomo + HiGHS MILP; OR-Tools routing; IBP optimizer semantics, TM re-routing) GREEN. Policy engine + approval UI (Python rules + web UI, Build Apps optional; mirrors Joule HITL guardrails) GREEN. IBP-shaped scenario service (CAP Node.js OData mock /IBP/API_SCENARIO + key figures) GREEN (mock). TM-shaped freight service (CAP OData V4 mock API_FREIGHTUNIT contract shape) GREEN (mock). Ariba-shaped risk service (CAP mock Risk Exposure API batch shape; up to 500 suppliers per call contract) GREEN (mock). Analytics + dashboard (SAC trial or web UI) YELLOW. Real tenant integration (BTP destination service + real OData) RED - Layer 3.

architecture.title: Three-layer design (Table 16)
architecture.details: Layer 1 - Hackfest MVP (Sept 23-29): 6 agents on LangGraph; 12-node synthetic pharma network; SimPy twin; Pyomo/HiGHS re-planner; policy engine + approval UI; CAP mocks of IBP/TM/Ariba; audit ledger; 10-min scripted demo. Purpose: win the rounds - a visible, working, governed loop. Layer 2 - Research platform (Oct-Dec 2026): RecoveryBench-12 scenarios + scoring harness; ablation across 4 baselines; GNN cascade module; resilience-score objective; paper drafts. Purpose: credibility - first recovery-decision benchmark + publication. Layer 3 - Startup product (2027+): real tenant connectors (BTP, OData); multi-tenant SaaS; proprietary signal fusion; pilot with 1-2 pharma exporters; provisional patent; pricing engine. Purpose: income - $15k-50k ACV mid-market SaaS with success fees. The layers share one codebase and one architecture; Layer 3 is primarily a connectors-and-hardening project, not a rebuild.

architecture.title: Sanjivani v2: five-agent lane-level cold-chain view
architecture.details: Version two upgrades the five-agent sketch in three ways: every predictive stage is bound to a named open model, the escalation ladder is explicit and severity-based, and the showcase scenario follows the 2026 research on where excursions really happen - the ground-handling dwell window. Five agents on SAP BTP: Sense Agent (ingests simulated IoT telemetry, lane and weather feeds, ground-handling events), Predict Agent (excursion-risk horizon using zero-shot time-series models), Scenario Agent (lane digital twin ranking recovery options by cost, risk and compliance), Act Agent (executes the approved play through carrier, warehouse and reefer interfaces), Comply Agent (writes the GDP-grade audit trail and CAPA-ready excursion dossier). Human-in-the-loop approval console gates only consequential actions; closed learning loop writes every outcome back into lane risk priors. (Note: the six-agent MVP roster A1-A6 in Ch.15 remains the build spec; the v2 five-agent sketch is the earlier lane-level view.)

agent_specifications.title: A1 - Disruption Sensing Agent
agent_specifications.details: Objective: detect candidate disruption events early with calibrated confidence. Inputs: news/geopolitical feeds; weather alerts; port status; tariff notices; GSCPI macro index; IoT telemetry. Outputs: candidate events (type, location, magnitude, confidence, provenance) to the event bus. Tools: feed readers; embedding model; NLP classifier; clustering. Memory: rolling 30-day signal history; source-reliability priors. Decision logic: threshold score with source cross-check - signals agreeing across 2+ source classes rise; single-source stay candidates. Failure modes: false positives (hoaxes, stale stories); missed slow-burn events; feed outages. Permissions: read-only on all data; can create candidate events only. Escalation: confidence > 0.6 hands to A2 for verification; below stays in watchlist.

agent_specifications.title: A2 - Event Verification & Scenario Agent
agent_specifications.details: Objective: debounce false positives and convert verified events into parameterized scenarios. Inputs: candidate events from A1; historical analog library; verifier prompts with cross-source retrieval. Outputs: verified events with confidence; 3/10/30-day scenarios (magnitude, duration, affected lanes) with probability weights. Tools: retrieval (GraphRAG on HANA); LLM scenario generation; analog-case library. Memory: library of past events + outcomes (grows with every loop). Decision logic: verification gate (2-source rule, staleness check, dedup); LLM drafts scenario parameters; parameters sanity-clamped by rules. Failure modes: hallucinated parameters; anchoring on recent events; conflicting sources. Permissions: writes scenarios; cannot trigger execution. Escalation: unverifiable high-impact events escalate to human analyst feed immediately.

agent_specifications.title: A3 - Network Impact Agent
agent_specifications.details: Objective: quantify what a scenario does to THIS network - SKUs, orders, service, cash. Inputs: verified scenarios; supply graph (HANA KG); open orders; inventory positions; lead times. Outputs: affected-node map; stockout probabilities per SKU-market; revenue-at-risk; cost impact bands. Tools: graph traversal (SPARQL/SQL); simulation hooks; calculator tools (no LLM math). Memory: network snapshot cache; per-customer elasticity priors. Decision logic: deterministic propagation on graph; Monte Carlo over scenario weights; all arithmetic in code, not in the LLM. Failure modes: stale master data; unknown second-tier dependencies; demand-model drift. Permissions: read-only. Escalation: impact above materiality threshold triggers A4 planning automatically.

agent_specifications.title: A4 - Logistics & Inventory Agent
agent_specifications.details: Objective: generate the best feasible recovery plan - re-route, re-source, re-allocate, re-book. Inputs: impact report; supplier alternatives (Ariba-shaped scores); carrier options; budget and policy caps. Outputs: ranked recovery strategies with cost/service/resilience scores; ready-to-post actions for approved plans. Tools: Pyomo+HiGHS MILP; OR-Tools routing; digital-twin strategy replay; LLM strategy drafting (structure only). Memory: strategy playbook; solver run history. Decision logic: LLM proposes strategy structures; optimizer computes feasible parameters; twin simulates each; multi-objective ranking (cost, service, resilience score). Failure modes: infeasible MILP (degrades to heuristic); solver timeout; bad input data from A3. Permissions: creates plans + solver calls (guardrailed); cannot post to SAP without A5 + human. Escalation: all plans above cost band escalate to human approval by design.

agent_specifications.title: A5 - Compliance & HITL Agent
agent_specifications.details: Objective: ensure every action is compliant, explainable, and human-approved where required. Inputs: recovery plan; policy rulebook (sanctions, tariffs, GDP, internal caps); supplier risk scores. Outputs: approved/blocked/modified plan with compliance annotations; approval requests with one-paragraph justifications. Tools: rules engine; sanctions/tariff checks; GDP checklist validator; approval workflow (UI + notification). Memory: policy version history; approval audit trail. Decision logic: rule validation precedes any human prompt; humans see simulation-backed context; denial loops back to A4 with constraints. Failure modes: rule conflicts (two policies disagree); approver fatigue (mitigated by tiering); stale policy files. Permissions: gatekeeper - only A5 can authorize execution posts. Escalation: conflicting policies or novel situations escalate to COO persona with full context packet.

agent_specifications.title: A6 - Audit & Learning Agent
agent_specifications.details: Objective: make every decision visible, replayable, and progressively smarter. Inputs: full event-reasoning-action-outcome chain; actuals (ETAs, costs, excursion outcomes). Outputs: immutable decision ledger; weekly prediction-vs-outcome scorecards; recalibrated thresholds and priors. Tools: append-only store; metrics calculators; drift monitors. Memory: the ledger IS the memory - decisions, not just data. Decision logic: post-action reconciliation of predicted vs actual; threshold updates proposed to humans (never self-applied). Failure modes: actuals gaps (missing ETA feedback); attribution ambiguity in multi-event periods. Permissions: append + propose; policy changes require human sign-off. Escalation: systematic prediction errors raise a 'model drift' ticket to the human team.

agent_specifications.title: Sixteen-role roster with tiering (Table 20)
agent_specifications.details: 1. Sensing Agent - continuous multi-source disruption detection - MVP (A1) - loop cannot start without it. 2. Event Verification Agent - credibility, dedup, staleness, confidence - MVP (inside A2) - false positives would torch credibility on stage. 3. Scenario Agent - 3/10/30-day parameterized futures - MVP (inside A2) - the theme's named Scenario Agent. 4. Supply-Chain Graph Agent - supplier-plant-warehouse-lane-customer mapping + cascade paths - MVP (A3) - impact reasoning is the GraphRAG wow. 5. Impact Prediction Agent - stockout probability, revenue-at-risk, service impact - MVP (A3) - quantified pain = rubric + ROI. 6. Inventory Agent - safety stock, redistribution, allocation - MVP (inside A4) - half the recovery decision. 7. Logistics Agent - re-routing, mode shift, freight re-booking - MVP (inside A4) - the visible SAP action. 8. Supplier Agent - alternative supplier evaluation (risk, price, lead time) - MVP (input to A4 via Ariba-shaped scores) - sourcing is the other half of recovery. 9. Procurement Agent - PO generation and sourcing events - MVP-lite (PO receipt only in demo) - full negotiation workflows are Future. 10. Optimization Agent - multi-objective solver orchestration - MVP (engine inside A4) - LLM-reasons, solver-decides principle. 11. Digital Twin / Simulation Agent - strategy replay before execution - MVP (engine band) - the demo's centerpiece comparison. 12. Compliance Agent - tariffs, sanctions, GDP, internal policy - MVP (A5) - the theme's named safeguard; zero-violation gate. 13. Human Approval Agent - risk-tiered gates and escalation - MVP (A5 gate UI) - governance is the thesis. 14. Execution Agent - posts to SAP-shaped APIs atomically - MVP (thin client in A4/A5 handoff) - receipts make it real. 15. Audit Agent - immutable decision trail - MVP (A6) - compliance product surface from day one. 16. Learning Agent - prediction-vs-outcome recalibration - MVP (scorecard view) then Advanced (auto-calibration) - full closed-loop learning is Layer 2 depth. Tiering rule: an agent ships early only if the visible loop breaks without it.

agent_specifications.title: Six MVP agents implement sixteen roles - body mapping
agent_specifications.details: Six MVP 'agents' implement sixteen envisioned roles because roles share bodies: A2 carries verification + scenario; A3 carries graph + impact; A4 carries inventory + logistics + supplier + optimization; A5 carries compliance + approval; A6 carries audit + learning. The architecture diagram shows all sixteen capabilities; the code shows six disciplined processes. In Q&A, that distinction is a strength - role coverage with implementation economy.

agent_specifications.title: FMEA snapshot (Table 19)
agent_specifications.details: 1. False disruption verified -> wasted replanning, alert fatigue returns; detection: A6 outcome tracking flags persistent false-verifies; mitigation: source-reliability priors down-weighted, verification threshold raised. 2. Missed disruption -> service failure with no plan; detection: A6 reconcile actuals vs no-event periods; mitigation: multi-source redundancy, macro-index (GSCPI) backstop. 3. LLM hallucinated scenario parameters -> infeasible or absurd plans; detection: rule clamps, solver infeasibility alarms; mitigation: parameters schema-validated, optimizer rejects out-of-bounds, A2 regenerates. 4. Agent loop / runaway tool-calls -> cost and latency blowout; detection: step-budget guard in LangGraph; mitigation: hard step + token caps, kill-switch to advisory mode. 5. Mock/API failure -> execution stalls mid-recovery; detection: health checks, transaction monitors; mitigation: compensating actions, advisory fallback, retry queue. 6. Human rejects good plan -> slower recovery than autonomous path; detection: A6 tracks override outcomes; mitigation: context quality improvements, override patterns feed policy tuning. 7. Prompt injection via news text -> manipulated recommendations; detection: sandboxed summarization, schema validation; mitigation: external text never parameterizes tools, allow-listed fields only. 8. Conflicting policies (tariff vs sanctions) -> compliant in one rule, violated in another; detection: A5 rule-conflict detector; mitigation: escalate to human with both rules cited, policy precedence table. Full register maintained in the build repo.

data_architecture.title: Core entities - knowledge graph schema sketch (Table 21)
data_architecture.details: Supplier: id, name, country, risk score (Ariba shape), capacity, lead time, single-source flag - source: Ariba-shaped mock + Kaggle disruption dataset priors. Plant/site: id, location, type (API/formulation/pack), capacity - synthetic network definition. Warehouse/hub: id, location, temperature class (2-8 C ambient), inventory positions - synthetic + IBP key-figure shapes. SKU/product: id, form (generic/biologic/vaccine), temp sensitivity, margin band, criticality - synthetic pharma catalog. Lane/route: origin, destination, mode, transit time, cost, disruption exposure flags - TM-shaped mock; Red Sea/Cape geometry. Port/node: id, country, congestion index, closure status - port-status feeds (demo), manual overrides. Tariff/policy: HS code, origin, rate, effective date, source URL - official gazette feeds (demo: curated file). DisruptionEvent: type, location, magnitude, confidence, provenance, window - A1/A2 agents (the graph grows at runtime). PurchaseOrder: supplier, SKU, qty, incoterm, status - IBP/S4-shaped mock. Shipment: lane, carrier, freight order id (TM shape), temp telemetry link, ETA - TM-shaped mock + simulated IoT stream. Customer/market: id, region, service-level target, demand forecast series - synthetic + Chronos/TimesFM forecast. DecisionRecord: event id, scenario, plan, approval, action, outcome, timestamps - A6 ledger (append-only). The graph is deliberately small for the MVP: 12 nodes that carry the whole story.

data_architecture.title: Three stores and the event bus
data_architecture.details: Three stores, three jobs. The relational core (HANA Cloud or PostgreSQL in dev) holds master data and open orders with typed schemas - the system of record the optimizers trust. The vector store (HANA vector engine) holds embedded event summaries and document chunks for semantic retrieval. The graph store (HANA knowledge graph engine; NetworkX in dev) holds the supply network and runtime DisruptionEvent nodes, enabling propagation queries. The event bus between agents is a lightweight queue (Redis Streams in dev; SAP Event Mesh shapes in the Layer-3 story). Every record carries provenance (source URL or system id), freshness (timestamp), and confidence (where computed) - the three metadata fields that make enterprise buyers take an AI system seriously.

evaluation_framework.title: Safety metrics and MVP targets

business_model.title: Company concept and ICP
business_model.details: Company concept: the post-alert decision layer for pharma supply chains - sold as 'the system that turns disruption alerts into approved, executed, audited recovery.' ICP: an Indian pharmaceutical or life-sciences exporter with $50m-500m revenue, an SAP or mid-market ERP backbone, 3-10 planning staff, regulated-market exposure (EU/US GDP), and a live scar from a disruption (a ruined cold-chain shipment, a demurrage bill, a missed tender). Buyer: VP Supply Chain or COO; user: planning team lead; compliance co-signer: QA/GDP. Segment reachable (industry associations, pharma clusters in Hyderabad/Ahmedabad, SAP's mid-market ecosystem), painful enough to buy, small enough that giants will not custom-serve it first - classic beachhead logic.

business_model.title: Business Model Canvas (Table 38)
business_model.details: Customer segments: primary Indian pharma exporters ($50-500m); secondary (Y2+) specialty chemicals, medical devices, auto components - all disruption-exposed, SAP-dense. Value propositions: minutes-not-weeks governed recovery; one prevented incident pays the year; GDP-grade audit trail for free; resilience score as a board-reportable KPI. Channels: SAP ecosystem (hackfest credibility, SAP Store listing path, partner-manager intros), pharma industry associations, college incubator networks, outbound to SC leaders on LinkedIn. Customer relationships: high-touch pilot to start (co-deploy with planning team), then quarterly business reviews with resilience scorecards; community of Indian SC planners for referrals. Revenue streams: tiered SaaS $18k / $36k / $60k ACV (by sites + lanes + event volume) + success fee (5-10% of verified prevented-loss value, capped) + onboarding fee; expansion modules (ColdSentry, AlertTriage) and API access. Key resources: the decision-outcome ledger (proprietary calibration data), RecoveryBench harness, solver-guardrail IP, SAP-integration expertise, the team's research credibility. Key activities: agent/twin/solver engineering, signal-source curation, compliance rulebook maintenance (per market), pilot delivery, benchmark publication. Key partners: SAP (startup programs, BTP), cold-chain IoT vendors (telemetry-in), freight forwarders (execution-in), patent counsel, college IPR cell, pharma industry body. Cost structure: team salaries (largest), cloud + LLM inference (modest, usage-based), signal APIs, legal/IP, sales travel; gross margin target 75-85%. One-page version (Ch.23.4, p.70): customer segments Indian pharma exporters $50-500m regulated markets; revenue $18k/$36k/$60k SaaS tiers + capped success fees.

business_model.title: Go-to-market and 1/3/5-year roadmap
business_model.details: GTM motion: paid pilot ($8k-15k, 8-10 weeks, one network, success criteria pre-written) -> convert to annual SaaS. Pilot sourcing: hackfest network, SAP partner intros, two warm pharma-cluster anchors. Year 1: 2 paid pilots, 1 conversion; provisional filed; RecoveryBench released; 1 paper submitted; revenue modest pilot income - goal is proof, not profit. Year 3: 10-14 customers in the beachhead; $1.5-3.5m ARR band (base case); module expansion; first EU-market compliance rulebook; team of 8-12; seed round optional (founders keep control if base case holds). Year 5: category position as 'the recovery layer' across life-sciences verticals; $6-12m ARR band (base); regional expansion (SEA generics exporters face identical dynamics); the ledger becomes the dataset competitors cannot synthesize.

business_model.title: Resilience Audit wedge - sellable next week
business_model.details: The smallest commercially viable product is already visible in Layer 1: a Resilience Audit-as-a-Service. Take one exporter's network snapshot, run the twelve-scenario benchmark against it, deliver a board-ready report: stockout probabilities per SKU-market under six disruption families, cost-at-risk quantified, prioritized resilience investment list. Needs no autonomous execution, no new integrations beyond a data extract; prices at $3k-6k - a consulting-style wedge that funds the SaaS journey, seeds the ledger with real networks, and creates the pilot pipeline. The autonomous loop sells after trust is established; the audit sells on day one.

business_model.title: Moat ranking (Table 39)
business_model.details: Decision-outcome ledger (what worked, at what cost): strength H, 18-24 months to build - generated only by running the loop on real networks; competitors cannot synthesize it. Solver-guardrail IP + patent portfolio: M-H, 12-18 months - deters feature-copying by alert vendors; requires professional review. Compliance rulebooks per market (GDP/tariff): M, 12 months - unsexy, cumulative, locally validated; enterprise buyers pay for exactly this. Benchmark + research credibility: M, 6-12 months - RecoveryBench positions the team as the category's measurement standard. SAP integration depth: M, ongoing - API-faithful connectors and A2A/MCP alignment; slows generic rivals more than SAP itself. Switching costs (ledger + rulebooks live in-tenant): M, per customer - data gravity grows with every event processed.

business_model.title: Why-customers-pay value anchors
business_model.details: Every customer conversation anchors on avoided loss: stockouts, expedited freight, excursion write-offs, demurrage, and planner overtime. A mid-size pharma exporter losing one biologics shipment (up to 20% of biologics shipments fail on temperature) can justify a $15k-50k ACV from a single prevented incident. One prevented biologics loss funds a year of the product; the audit trail is a compliance deliverable they currently produce by hand.

financial_model.title: Customer ROI equation and benchmark rates
financial_model.details: V = V_stockout + V_expedite + V_excursion + V_inventory + V_labor. V_stockout = P_incidents x L_days x daily_margin_at_risk x reduction_rate. V_expedite = expedited_spend x reduction_rate (benchmark 15-25%). V_excursion = excursion_writeoffs x prevention_rate (benchmark 30-60% with governed response). V_inventory = buffer_inventory_value x carrying_cost_rate x optimization_gain (benchmark 5-10%). V_labor = planner_hours_per_event x events x hourly_cost x automation_rate (benchmark 70-90%).

qa_war_room.title: Q1: Is this not just a ChatGPT wrapper?
qa_war_room.details: No - the LLM never makes the math decisions. Solvers (Pyomo/HiGHS, OR-Tools) compute feasible plans; the twin simulates them; the LLM orchestrates, explains and drafts scenarios. Wrap a chatbot around a dashboard and you get text; wrap agents around solvers and you get governed action.

qa_war_room.title: Q2: Your SAP integration is mocked. Is that honest?
qa_war_room.details: Yes, and deliberately: student accounts cannot hold IBP/TM tenants. We implement the released, documented API contracts (IBP /IBP/API_SCENARIO, TM API_FREIGHTUNIT V4, Ariba Risk Exposure) as CAP services, so porting to a real tenant is configuration, not re-architecture. HANA Cloud is real, not mocked.

qa_war_room.title: Q3: How do you prevent hallucinated decisions?
qa_war_room.details: Three walls: external text never parameterizes tools; all numeric parameters are schema-validated and rule-clamped; every plan passes the policy engine before a human sees it. The LLM proposes structure; deterministic systems approve feasibility.

qa_war_room.title: Q4: What happens when the AI is wrong?
qa_war_room.details: The same thing that happens when a planner is wrong - except bounded and recorded: risk-tiered approval, budget caps, compensating actions, and a full audit ledger. Advisory mode is the fail-safe: the system can degrade to recommendations only.

qa_war_room.title: Q5: Everstream or Blue Yonder could build this in a quarter. Why you?
qa_war_room.details: They could - eventually. Incumbents monetize the pre-decision layer; adding governed execution competes with their own alert products (cannibalization). Startups die of the opposite problem: no distribution. We are building the layer neither has an incentive to ship first, and SAP Hackfest is exactly the distribution event for it.

qa_war_room.title: Q6: How is this different from SAP's own Joule agents?
qa_war_room.details: SAP's agents optimize tasks inside processes - Joule for supply chain shipped GA in Q1 2026. We are the cross-system recovery loop that orchestrates across IBP, TM and Ariba with governance - the layer SAP itself invites via A2A/MCP for third-party agents. We ride their roadmap rather than duplicate it.

qa_war_room.title: Q7: Where does your data come from?
qa_war_room.details: Free/open signals (news, weather, port status, tariff gazettes, GSCPI), customer master data (their SAP), and - the moat - the decision-outcome ledger our own loop generates. No proprietary feed dependencies.

qa_war_room.title: Q8: Are you claiming a patent?
qa_war_room.details: No. We have three white-space hypotheses (closed loop, alert triage, GDP-aware response) from preliminary screening, and a plan to file a provisional after professional review - before public disclosure. We explicitly do not claim patentability today.

qa_war_room.title: Q9: What is the market size, honestly?
qa_war_room.details: Gartner: agentic SCM spend under $2bn (2025) growing to $53bn (2030); SCRM software $5-8bn growing 9-14% CAGR; disruption costs $184bn/yr create the willingness to pay. SOM sized bottom-up: about 1,300 mid-size Indian pharma and specialty exporters, initial serviceable target a few hundred.

qa_war_room.title: Q10: Who pays? Procurement will squeeze you.
qa_war_room.details: The VP Supply Chain owns the budget (loss-avoidance line, not efficiency line); QA/GDP co-signs because the audit trail is a compliance product. Priced $15k-50k ACV mid-market with success fees on prevented losses - ROI from one prevented biologics incident pays the year.

qa_war_room.title: Q11: Cold chain IoT needs sensors. Do you sell hardware?
qa_war_room.details: No hardware - that would disqualify us in the regional round and distract the company. We ingest existing telemetry (Tive/Controlant/Sensitech-class devices already deployed); where none exists, simulated streams in the demo.

qa_war_room.title: Q12: Your 11-minutes-vs-11-days number - real or marketing?
qa_war_room.details: Measured on our 12-scenario benchmark: manual baseline is timed from case-study evidence (weeks); our loop is instrumented (signal-in to execution-receipts). We show the methodology and the harness, and we label the manual baseline as a reconstruction, not a stopwatch run.

qa_war_room.title: Q13: Six agents - why not one big agent?
qa_war_room.details: One agent doing sensing, planning and compliance is un-auditable and un-testable. Specialized agents map to accountability (who approved what), to failure isolation, and to the official theme's own agent families. Multi-agent failure modes are exactly what our FMEA and ledger address.

qa_war_room.title: Q14: What if two agents disagree?
qa_war_room.details: They are designed to: A4 proposes, A5 validates. Conflicts resolve by policy precedence, then by human escalation with both rules cited. Disagreement is a feature - it is how the system surfaces trade-offs instead of hiding them.

qa_war_room.title: Q15: Does the human gate not destroy the autonomy story?
qa_war_room.details: It IS the autonomy story that enterprises will buy. Gartner cancels ungoverned projects; SAP's own HITL framing agrees. Our tiers mean low-risk actions never wait for a human - autonomy where safe, oversight where it matters.

qa_war_room.title: Q16: Startup while studying?
qa_war_room.details: The three-layer design separates hackfest (1 week), research (1 semester), startup (post-graduation or with incubator support). College IPR cells and SAP's startup ecosystem programs exist for exactly this path. We are not promising a company next month - we are building compounding assets now.

qa_war_room.title: Q17: Why pharma and not something bigger like retail?
qa_war_room.details: Bigger markets have bigger incumbents and weaker per-incident pain. Pharma has: documented $35bn cold-chain losses, mandatory GDP documentation, life-critical stakes that fit the theme's human-cost framing, and an Indian beachhead we can physically access. Depth first, breadth later.

qa_war_room.title: Q18: What is your unit economics?
qa_war_room.details: Mid-market SaaS benchmarks: $15k-50k ACV, gross margin 75-85% (LLM + cloud costs per customer are modest), CAC low through SAP ecosystem channels and hackfest credibility. Detailed three-scenario model in the financial chapter.

qa_war_room.title: Q19: Data privacy - you see customers' supplier networks?
qa_war_room.details: The graph lives in the customer's tenant (HANA) or a dedicated namespace; our agents process, the customer owns. We never cross-train customer networks - the ledger improves thresholds per-tenant, not a global model on their data.

qa_war_room.title: Q20: What did you personally build vs generate?
qa_war_room.details: Fair question in 2026: every component is in a public repo with our commits; the architecture, FMEA, benchmark design and this dossier are original work; AI tools accelerated code, as professional teams do. We can open any file and explain any line - invite us to.

qa_war_room.title: Q21: Red Sea is old news. What is next?
qa_war_room.details: Structural disruption is the point: tariff volatility 'for years, not months' (Columbus Consulting), canal climate risk, 22 critical risks flagged for 2026 (z2data). Our scenario library refreshes quarterly from live signals - the demo story ages, the mechanism does not.

qa_war_room.title: Q22: How accurate is your sensing?
qa_war_room.details: Calibrated, not perfect: verification uses a 2-source rule with confidence scoring; A6 measures prediction-vs-outcome every week. We publish the miss/false-positive rates in the research layer instead of claiming magic.

qa_war_room.title: Q23: Why not just buy IBP's optimizer?
qa_war_room.details: IBP's optimizer plans within IBP's cycle. We orchestrate across systems, add external signals IBP does not ingest, and wrap decisions in cross-system governance. Several of our modules are explicitly IBP-complementary - DemandShield is essentially 'IBP scenarios, automated.'

qa_war_room.title: Q24: Scale - can this run a 10,000-SKU network?
qa_war_room.details: The MVP proves the pattern on 12 SKUs. Complexity grows with graph size, and the solver stack (HiGHS/OR-Tools) handles industrial instances; the honest roadmap is pilot at exporter scale (hundreds of SKUs) before enterprise scale. We say so on stage.

qa_war_room.title: Q25: Security of an autonomous system with SAP credentials?
qa_war_room.details: Least-privilege service accounts per action class; no interactive credentials; policy-engine authorization on every call; full action ledger; kill-switch to advisory mode. Agent permissions are a designed feature (Chapter 12), not an afterthought.

qa_war_room.title: Q26: What is your worst weakness?
qa_war_room.details: Data on real recovery outcomes: our benchmark is synthetic until a pilot generates actuals. That is why Layer 2 (research platform) exists - and why we want a pilot customer more than we want prize money.

qa_war_room.title: Q27: Team - who does what?
qa_war_room.details: Five roles, named: agent architecture, SAP/BTP, optimization/data science, full-stack, research/business lead - with exact build lists in the implementation chapter. No passengers; the demo is live, not delegated.

qa_war_room.title: Q28: Regulatory risk - can an AI legally adjust pharma shipments?
qa_war_room.details: A regulated company's qualified person remains accountable - that is why the GDP investigation record and human gate are core features, not options. We automate the documentation burden, not the accountability.

qa_war_room.title: Q29: Why 'SANJEEVANI'?
qa_war_room.details: In Indian legend, Sanjeevani is the herb that restores life. A supply chain for medicine that heals itself - the name does the pitch. Global-facing product name is a decision for the startup layer.

qa_war_room.title: Q30: What would make us remember you tomorrow?
qa_war_room.details: The 11-second approval click on stage; the ledger writing itself in front of judges; and the sentence: 'SAP sells the immune system - we demonstrated the antibody.' Ask us anything; the war room has thirty more answers.

research_roadmap.title: Research question and hypotheses (H-R1, H-R2)
research_roadmap.details: Research question: can a governed multi-agent LLM system - sensing, scenario generation, simulation, solver-orchestrated re-planning and human approval - recover disrupted pharmaceutical supply chains measurably better than rule-based planning and single-agent baselines, without violating policy constraints? H-R1: the multi-agent-plus-twin-plus-governance configuration reduces recovery cost and service-level loss versus all baselines across a 12-scenario benchmark, while producing zero policy violations; the ablation will show that the digital twin and the governance gate each contribute measurably (removing the twin degrades cost efficiency; removing the gate increases constraint violations). H-R2: weak-signal scenario parameters generated with retrieval-grounded LLMs outperform naive heuristic scenarios on recovery outcomes at equal solver budgets.

research_roadmap.title: RecoveryBench-12 benchmark contribution
research_roadmap.details: The field has a monitoring benchmark (January 2026) and no recovery-decision benchmark. RecoveryBench-12: twelve replayable disruption scenarios on a fixed synthetic pharma network, each with a seeded ground-truth recovery envelope (feasible cost floor, minimum service level, policy constraints) and a scoring harness that computes recovery cost, time-to-recover, fill rate, policy violations and decision-trace completeness for any system that conforms to a simple event-plan-outcome interface. Scenarios derive from the Chapter 2 case families (maritime closure, tariff shock, supplier failure, cold-chain excursion, port strike, demand surge, and combinations), with parameters perturbed to prevent overfitting. Dataset, harness and baselines released openly.

research_roadmap.title: Four-baseline experimental design (Table 36)
research_roadmap.details: A. Rule-based planning: safety-stock + expedites triggered by thresholds; no ML, no agents - isolates the value of intelligence itself. B. Single agent: one LLM agent with tools (no twin, no governance) - isolates multi-agent decomposition value. C. Multi-agent: A1-A6 without twin simulation (LLM plans directly) - isolates digital-twin value. D. Full SANJEEVANI: multi-agent + twin + optimization + governance gate - the complete loop; D vs C isolates governance + optimization effect.

research_roadmap.title: Metrics, ablations and paper plan
research_roadmap.details: Metrics: recovery cost (vs feasible floor), time-to-recover (signal-in to plan-executed), service level over the 30-day horizon, policy violations (must be zero for D), decision-trace completeness, human-attention cost (approval clicks per event). Ablations: remove twin (D vs C); remove gate (D vs an ungoverned D); swap LLM tier (small vs large model); perturb scenario parameters to test overfitting. Paper skeleton: Abstract, Introduction, Problem, Related Work, Research Gap, Architecture, Methodology, Experimental Setup, Results, Ablation, Safety/Governance, Limitations, Future Work, Conclusion. Candidate titles: (1) Governed Recovery: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Self-Healing Pharmaceutical Supply Chains; (2) RecoveryBench: A Replayable Benchmark for Supply-Chain Recovery Decisions by Agentic AI; (3) LLM Agents that Call Solvers Safely: Guardrails for Autonomous Supply-Chain Re-planning; (4) From Weak Signals to Executed Recovery: Closing the Agentic Supply-Chain Loop; (5) Resilience as an Objective: Optimizing Time-to-Recover under Human Oversight. Venues (student-realistic first): institute symposium and national student conferences; IEEE ICRA/IROS workshops on agentic systems; AAAI/IJCAI workshop tracks; INFORMS Applied Analytics; journals: Computers & Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain Management: An International Journal.

research_roadmap.title: Round 1 pitch structure (Table 24)
research_roadmap.details: Round 1 evaluates ideas on four scored dimensions - Persona (0-2), Problem Statement Clarity (0-2), User Needs Identification (0-2), Solution Alignment (0-2) - within a 15-minute slot (10 pitch + 5 Q&A), with learning-journey grounding from SAP Learning Hub expected. 10 slides: 1 Title + tagline (0:30); 2 Persona: Meera (1:15); 3 A day the world fractured - Red Sea +10-14 days, 417% freight spike (1:30); 4 The real gap - alert-to-recovery delta (1:00); 5 What Meera needs - N1-N7 (1:15); 6 Solution: the loop (1:30); 7 Built on SAP, free-tier honest (1:00); 8 Proof in numbers - 11 minutes vs 11 days; -23% recovery cost; 100% audit (1:00); 9 Beyond the hackfest (1:00); 10 Close (0:30). What judges remember 24 hours later: one persona with a name and verbatim quote; one number pair (11 minutes vs 11 days); one visible human gate; one vendor-mirrored sentence - 'sense, decide, act - governed.'

glossary.title: Glossary of key terms and acronyms (Table B.1)
glossary.details: Agent (AI): a software process that perceives state, plans, and takes actions via tools under a policy; here, a specialized node in a LangGraph state machine. A2A / MCP: Agent2Agent protocol and Model Context Protocol - interoperability standards for agent communication and tool/data access; SAP-endorsed (2025-2026). ACV: annual contract value. BTP: SAP Business Technology Platform (free tier used here). CAP: SAP Cloud Application Programming Model - framework used to build the API-faithful mock services. DE Mosul / DES: discrete-event simulation - deterministic replay of network flows over time (SimPy). Digital twin: a computable replica of the supply network used to replay scenarios before committing decisions. FEU: forty-foot equivalent unit - container size used in freight-rate quotes. GDP: Good Distribution Practice - pharmaceutical distribution quality rules (EU/WHO/US) requiring documented excursion investigation. GraphRAG: retrieval-augmented generation grounded in a knowledge graph plus vector search (SAP HANA pattern). GSCPI: Global Supply Chain Pressure Index (New York Fed) - monthly macro disruption pressure measure. HITL: human-in-the-loop - risk-tiered human approval gates inside the autonomous loop. HS code: Harmonized System commodity code - the key on which tariff schedules apply. IBP: SAP Integrated Business Planning - demand/S&OP/response/inventory planning suite. KSM / API: key starting material / active pharmaceutical ingredient - upstream chemical inputs (India: 70-90% China dependency). LangGraph: MIT-licensed agent orchestration framework with checkpointing and native human-in-the-loop interrupts. MILP: mixed-integer linear programming - the optimization class used for re-planning (Pyomo + HiGHS). OData: Open Data Protocol - REST-based API standard used by SAP products (IBP/TM shapes mocked with identical contracts). Resilience score: composite measure (time-to-recover, fill rate, cost-at-risk) used as an audited objective in re-planning. RTTVP: real-time transportation visibility platform - the project44/FourKites category. SCRM: supply chain risk management (software market category). TTR / TTS: time-to-recover / time-to-survive - Ivanov-school resilience metrics. Zero-shot forecasting: time-series prediction by pretrained foundation models without per-customer training (Chronos, TimesFM).

workflow_specifications.title: Team architecture (workflow Ch.1)
workflow_specifications.details: Project: SANJEEVANI - The Self-Healing Pharma Supply Chain Network. Core principle: Sense -> Verify -> Understand -> Scenario -> Simulate -> Optimize -> Approve -> Execute -> Audit -> Learn. Architecture rule: six disciplined MVP agents implement the required capabilities; do not turn the conceptual 16-role roster into 16 independent agents. The team works in one Git repository; each member owns a vertical slice; all three integrate through explicit JSON/Pydantic-style contracts; the critical path is one polished end-to-end demo. Member 1: Sense + Verify + Scenario + Network Impact - 'What happened and what is affected?' - agents A1, A2, A3. Member 2: Digital Twin + Recovery + Optimization + Routing - 'What should we do?' - agent A4. Member 3: Compliance + HITL + SAP execution + Audit/Learning + UI - 'Can we safely execute it?' - agents A5, A6. Important: A2 combines verification + scenario; A3 combines graph + impact; A4 combines inventory/logistics/supplier/optimization; A5 combines compliance + approval; A6 combines audit + learning - the dossier's intended MVP compression.

workflow_specifications.title: Shared repository structure and ownership matrix (workflow Ch.2)
workflow_specifications.details: Repo tree: sanjeevani/ - README.md, .env.example, requirements.txt, package.json; config/ (settings.yaml, policies.yaml, scenarios.yaml); data/ (network/, products/, suppliers/, shipments/, events/, telemetry/); backend/ (agents/, simulation/, optimization/, governance/, sap/, audit/, api/); frontend/; tests/; scripts/; docs/; demo/. Ownership: data/ M1 OWNER; agents/sensing+verification+scenario+impact M1 OWNER; graph/ M1 OWNER; simulation/ M2 OWNER; optimization/+routing/ M2 OWNER; governance/ M3 OWNER; sap/ M3 OWNER; audit/+learning/ M3 OWNER; frontend/ M3 OWNER; api/ M3 OWNER; config/contracts/tests/docs SHARED by all.

workflow_specifications.title: Member 1 spec (workflow Ch.4)
workflow_specifications.details: Mission: build the upstream intelligence layer - convert raw signals into a verified disruption, scenario, network impact, and machine-readable handoff to Member 2. Own: A1 Sensing; A2 Verification & Scenario; A3 Network Impact; synthetic pharma network; event data; graph/network reasoning; confidence/provenance; impact report. Do NOT own: recovery optimization, SAP execution, approval UI. Workflow: signals -> normalize -> classify -> verify/deduplicate -> confidence/staleness -> create scenario -> traverse network -> calculate affected shipments/products -> calculate stockout/service/revenue risk -> emit Impact contract. Implementation order: 1. deterministic synthetic 12-node pharma network (suppliers, plants, ports, warehouses, lanes, customers); 2. scripted disruption feeds - Red Sea closure and biologics temperature excursion, all demo inputs deterministic/offline; 3. Sensing Agent - ingestion, normalization, event typing, source metadata; 4. Verification - confidence, deduplication, freshness/staleness, severity; 5. Scenario Agent - parameterized 3/10/30-day scenario objects; 6. Network Impact - graph traversal and affected-node/shipments calculation; 7. impact metrics - revenue-at-risk, stockout probability, service-level risk; 8. one clean function/API returning the shared Impact object; 9. unit tests and one integration fixture consumed by Member 2. Acceptance: deterministic detection of the seeded event; confidence/provenance/freshness fields; reproducible impact; output validates against shared Impact schema; Member 2 runs the module without private internals; every UI number traceable to source data or deterministic calculation.

workflow_specifications.title: Member 2 spec (workflow Ch.5)
workflow_specifications.details: Mission: take Member 1's quantified impact and determine the best recovery plan using deterministic simulation and mathematical optimization. Own: A4 Recovery; SimPy digital twin; three recovery strategies; Pyomo + HiGHS MILP; OR-Tools routing; cost/service/resilience/temperature-risk calculations. Do NOT own: event sensing, final compliance gate, SAP API implementation, frontend. Workflow: impact -> construct disrupted network state -> replay baseline -> simulate WAIT / REROUTE VIA MUMBAI + AIR / EMERGENCY SOURCE -> calculate KPIs -> optimize -> select best feasible plan -> emit RecoveryPlan. Implementation order: 1. consume Impact contract via fixture first; 2. deterministic SimPy digital twin for the 12-node network; 3. baseline WAIT strategy; 4. REROUTE VIA MUMBAI + AIR; 5. EMERGENCY SOURCE; 6. objective terms - recovery cost, service level, resilience score, temperature risk; 7. Pyomo/HiGHS optimization with explicit constraints and bounds - the LLM must not perform the math; 8. OR-Tools routing only where it materially supports the demo route decision; 9. ranked strategy table plus one RecoveryPlan object; 10. deterministic tests for feasibility, objective calculation, repeatability. Acceptance: all three strategies run from same scenario input; same seed same results; optimizer never violates hard constraints; recommended plan validates against RecoveryPlan schema; strategy table has enough data for UI cost/service/risk/resilience; no LLM-generated number treated as authoritative when a deterministic engine can calculate it.

workflow_specifications.title: Member 3 spec (workflow Ch.6)
workflow_specifications.details: Mission: turn the optimized recovery plan into a governed business action - validate it, ask for human approval, execute through SAP-shaped mocks, produce an auditable result. Own: A5 Compliance + HITL; CAP mocks for IBP/TM/Ariba; execution receipts; A6 Audit + Learning; React/Vite dashboard; approval screen; demo orchestration API. Do NOT own: core optimization mathematics or upstream event detection. Workflow: RecoveryPlan -> policy validation -> compliance checks -> risk tier -> approval card -> human approval -> SAP-shaped execution -> receipts -> audit ledger -> outcome/learning panel. Implementation order: 1. backend API/orchestrator consuming a RecoveryPlan fixture; 2. policy engine - budget caps, parameter bounds, sanctions/trade/GDP-style checks, approval rules; 3. approval state machine - consequential actions pause for human approval; 4. CAP Node.js mocks shaped like IBP scenario, TM freight, Ariba risk/procurement contracts; 5. execution client with transactional sequencing and visible receipts; 6. append-only decision ledger - event, reasoning metadata, scenario, recommendation, approval, action, outcome; 7. learning/outcome view comparing predicted vs actual with recalibration notice - no pretended autonomous model retraining in MVP; 8. dashboard - loop HUD, network map, impact KPIs, strategy table, compliance panel, approval card, execution receipts, audit/learning; 9. offline demo mode and one-command reset; 10. integrate all three members and freeze the demo path. Acceptance: every execution blocked until required approval; compliance failure prevents execution and explains why; IBP/TM/Ariba mocks return deterministic receipts; audit record for every major loop stage; frontend renders the complete journey from one seeded scenario; demo runs without venue Wi-Fi or live APIs.

workflow_specifications.title: Integration flow and rule (workflow Ch.7)
workflow_specifications.details: MEMBER 1: Signal -> Verification -> Scenario -> Network Impact -> Impact JSON. MEMBER 2: Digital Twin -> WAIT / REROUTE / EMERGENCY SOURCE -> Optimization -> RecoveryPlan JSON. MEMBER 3: Policy -> Compliance -> Human Approval -> IBP + TM + Ariba mocks -> Execution Receipts -> Audit Ledger -> Learning / Outcome -> Dashboard. Integration rule: each member must be able to test their portion with a frozen fixture from the previous member; do not block development waiting for the previous module; once the real module is ready, swap the fixture for the live call and run contract tests.

workflow_specifications.title: Git / collaboration rules and commit format (workflow Ch.8)
workflow_specifications.details: main is always runnable. Branches: member1-ai, member2-optimization, member3-sap-ui. Pull/rebase or merge latest main before integration work. Small commits; one logical change per commit. Never commit secrets, API keys, .env files, generated databases or huge model files. Every PR must include: what changed, files changed, tests run, integration impact, rollback note. Breaking contract changes require all three members to agree before merge. After Sep 27, no architecture changes unless required for a critical bug. Suggested commit format: feat(sensing): add disruption ingestion; feat(impact): add network risk calculation; feat(twin): add deterministic replay; feat(optimizer): add recovery MILP; feat(policy): add compliance gate; feat(sap): add TM mock execution; feat(ui): add approval console; test(integration): verify recovery contract.

workflow_specifications.title: Definition of Done (workflow Ch.10)
workflow_specifications.details: Functional: one complete deterministic scenario runs from signal to audit. Governed: no consequential SAP-shaped action bypasses policy + human approval. Explainable: every recommendation has visible reasons and numerical evidence. Reproducible: seeded data and offline mode produce the same demo result. Integrated: all shared contracts validate automatically. Demoable: presenter can reset the system and rerun the scenario quickly. web_regulatory_verification.title: WHO TRS 961 Annex 9 primary text
web_regulatory_verification.details: WHO TRS 961, Annex 9: Model guidance for the storage and transport of time- and temperature-sensitive pharmaceutical products (2011) - principal requirements for safe storage and distribution of TTSPPs; Supplement 8 covers temperature mapping of storage areas (TechNet-21, updated Mar 2025); Dickson: Annex 9 aligns with GDP including pre-qualified cold-chain packaging.

web_regulatory_verification.title: USP <1079> chapter family
web_regulatory_verification.details: USP General Chapter <1079> 'Good Storage and Shipping Practices' provides risk-based guidance for storing/distributing/shipping Pharmacopeial preparations; the <1079> series applies to organizations involved in drug product storage and transportation; <1079.4> 'Temperature Mapping for Storage Areas' (13 pages) focuses on qualification of storage areas to maintain temperature.

web_regulatory_verification.title: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 scope
web_regulatory_verification.details: 21 CFR Part 11 applies to records in electronic form that are created, modified, maintained, archived, retrieved, or transmitted under any records requirements set by FDA regulations (guidance scope, Aug 24 2018); governs electronic records/electronic signatures for temperature-monitoring records kept electronically (eCFR current text available).

web_regulatory_verification.title: CDSCO GDP guidelines (India)
web_regulatory_verification.details: CDSCO guidance document list includes 'Guidelines on good distribution practices for pharmaceutical Products' dated 2024-Apr-02 (783 KB) - matches the dossier's 'GDP.PP Ver. 00 Apr 2024'; a draft GDP guidance circulated Aug 2024; industry advocacy around July 2024 draft rules with enforcement messaging through Aug 2025.

web_ai_stack.title: TimesFM (Google) licensing & versions

web_ai_stack.details: TimesFM is Google Research's pretrained time-series foundation model: source code Apache-2.0 and model weights up to version 2.5 Apache-2.0; TimesFM-3 enables zero-shot multivariate forecasting in a single forward pass via BigQuery ML (preview Jun 12 2026); HN discussion references the 200M-parameter model; weights on Hugging Face.

web_ai_stack.details: Chronos family of pretrained time-series forecasting models is Apache-2.0 licensed; chronos-t5-large on Hugging Face (Mar 2024); package chronos-forecasting 1.5.1 on PyPI; Chronos-Bolt available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart; Chronos-2 extends from univariate to universal forecasting with cross-learning; production case: Deutsche Bahn forecasting (AWS, May 7 2025).

web_ai_stack.details: Salesforce Moirai 2.0 is a decoder-only universal time-series forecasting transformer; moirai-2.0-R-small is licensed cc-by-nc-4.0 on Hugging Face - NON-commercial, a licensing gotcha vs Apache-2.0 alternatives; the Uni2TS PyTorch library is MIT; Moirai-MoE paper (2024) cited 222 times; Salesforce publishes fine-tuning guidance for business time series (Jan 8 2026).

web_ai_stack.title: Multi-agent framework comparison & licenses
web_ai_stack.value_raw: CrewAI: MIT, Python >=3.10, v1.2.0 (May 2026); LangGraph: state-machine, best for stateful workflows; AutoGen: conversation-based
web_ai_stack.details: 2026 framework consensus: LangGraph enforces a state machine and is the best pick for explicit stateful workflows; CrewAI (MIT license, Python >=3.10, v1.2.0 as of May 2026) is the fastest route to role-based multi-agent collaboration; AutoGen treats work as conversation and fits research-style coordination; production comparisons weigh state management, observability, human-in-the-loop recovery (Aug 2026 analyses).

web_ai_stack.title: Time-series benchmark landscape
web_ai_stack.details: GIFT-Eval (Salesforce, Nov 12 2024) is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating general time-series forecasting models, particularly foundation models; the influential 'Are Transformers Effective for Time Series Forecasting?' work (HF, Jun 2023) showed simple linear models (DLinear) can beat transformers - relevant caveat when picking forecast models for demand sensing.

web_demo_feeds.title: Open-Meteo weather API
web_demo_feeds.details: Open-Meteo is an open-source weather API offering free access for non-commercial use with NO API key required - immediate use for lane weather sensing in the demo; Historical Forecast API archives comprehensive data (incl. atmospheric pressure levels) from all accessible forecast models. Alternative: OpenWeather provides current/forecast/historical/air-quality APIs (key required).

web_demo_feeds.title: AIS vessel tracking feed
web_demo_feeds.details: aisstream.io is a free API to stream global AIS data via websockets - tracks vessel position, identity and port calls; suitable for port-arrival sensing in the demo without paid AIS subscriptions.

web_demo_feeds.title: Freight rate data access
web_demo_feeds.details: Freightos operates the Baltic Freight Index (FBX) and provides rate data through its WebCargo platform (strength: ocean freight); FBX is the global benchmark for container freight rates with weekly assessments across major tradelanes (apis.io catalog); Freightos air freight APIs connect forwarder rate management to TMS/sales portals.

web_demo_feeds.title: GDELT global news event feed
web_demo_feeds.details: GDELT is a free and open platform monitoring broadcast, print and web news from nearly every corner of the world; two main databases: Event Database and Global Knowledge Graph; free cloud-based Analysis Service plus DOC 2.0 full-text search API (debuted Jun 2017); python newsfeed tooling queries GDELT Events and extracts article full text - ideal free disruption-news sensor for the demo.

web_demo_feeds.title: BLE temperature loggers (IoT sensing)
web_demo_feeds.details: Consumer/prosumer BLE (Bluetooth) temperature loggers usable as demo IoT sensors: Prosensor intemp cold-chain Bluetooth recorders (temperature, humidity, brightness display, external channel, glycol-bottle variants); Sopalog BLE connects continuously-measuring loggers to smartphone/tablet; waterproof Bluetooth temperature+brightness recorders available - a practical substitute for pharma-grade ELINA/La-Rue class loggers in hackathon demos.
